title: Protocol for resolving enzyme orientation and dynamics in advanced porous materials via SDSL-EPR
protocol: Create plasmids with the needed mutants.
Dissolve ordered primers in sterilized water following standard PCR procedure.
Include cysteine-free, pseudo-wildtype plasmid of the protein in the plasmid using PCR procedure.
Mutate native free cysteines in the target protein to serine or alanine.
Transform plasmid into cells via mini-prep using standard procedure and commercial kit.
Confirm sequence of plasmid via commercial DNA sequencing service.
Store resultant DNA at -20°C for further use.
Transform mutants into solid LB medium plates with minor modifications.
Inoculate one colony from the plate into 25 mL LB (1 × AMP) medium.
Grow the inoculated culture at 37°C for 12-16 hours under shaking at 205-225 rpm.
Add the overnight culture to 1 L of LB (1 × AMP) medium and incubate at 37°C with shaking for 4 hours.
Induce each liter of cells with 1 mL of 1 M IPTG at 37°C under shaking for 1.5 hours.
Harvest the induced cells via centrifugation at 4000 rpm for 15-45 minutes.
Resuspend the cell pellets in 25-50 mL of lysate buffer and shake gently.
Sonicate the resuspended pellets on ice with a 50% duty cycle for 5 minutes.
Let the sonicated sample rest on ice for 5 minutes.
Centrifuge the sample at 15,000 rpm at 4°C for 1 hour to separate supernatant from debris.
Filter the supernatant through a 0.22 μm filter to remove large particles or pellets.
Equilibrate FPLC motors with lysate buffer.
Load the filtered supernatant onto a GE ion-exchange (SP HP) column.
Rinse the column with lysate buffer until UV absorbance is near zero and collect flow-through.
Elute the column with varied salt content: from 0% to 10% in 2 minutes, from 10% to 30% in 10 minutes, from 30% to 100% in 0.5 minutes, and wash with 100% for 50 mL.
Collect the protein fraction between 15% and 25%.
Add DTT to the solution before running the desalting column to prevent protein dimerization due to disulfide bond formation between cysteines.
Equilibrate the desalting column with spin labeling buffer (100 mL without DTT).
Load cysteine mutants into the desalting column.
Collect the protein as it appears in the first peak (12 mL).
Immediately add HO-225 to the collected protein in a 10-fold excess relative to the cysteine mutant concentration.
Cover the container with foil and incubate at 4°C overnight.
Remove unreacted HO-225 from the mixture using Amicon concentrators with a 10 kDa cutoff via filtration-centrifugation.
Concentrate or dilute the protein solution using Amicon concentrators to achieve a concentration of approximately 0.2–0.5 mM for storage at 4°C.
Confirm the molecular weight and yield of the spin-labeled protein by gel electrophoresis following standard procedures.
Confirm the secondary structure of the spin labeled protein by Circular Dichroism.
Confirm the activity of the spin labeled protein using the standard lysozyme activity kit available at Sigma-Aldrich.
Optional: Mix an aliquot of 0.5 mL cells with 0.5 mL sterilized glycerol uniformly and store at −20 or −80°C for future expression.
Store labeled proteins at −20°C for long-term storage.
Resuspend MOF/COF in HEPES buffer (pH 7.0–7.4).
Mix labeled protein with resuspended MOF/COF and shake gently for overnight at room temperature.
Use 1 mg of MOF/COF and 1-2 mg of protein to ensure excess protein for loading.
Adjust conditions if needed, considering lower temperatures or alternative buffers like acetate or MES buffer.
Mix metal ion (Zn2+ or Ca2+) and ligand with enzyme in water or MeOH.
Allow co-precipitation overnight with gentle shaking if desired.
Remove unwanted species.
Centrifuge at 14,000 rpm for 5 minutes to remove free protein, metal, and ligand.
Resuspend the enzyme@MOF/COF pellets with water.
Centrifuge again as needed until no residual protein and ligand remain in the supernatant, which can be determined via UV-vis absorption spectroscopy.
Store resultant enzyme@MOF materials at 4°C in water or MeOH.
Confirm the integrity of the materials and the function of the enzyme.

Carry out standard MOF/COF characterization such as scanning electron microscope (SEM), powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD), thermal gravimetric analysis (TGA), and N2 absorption experiments to confirm the loading of the enzyme and structure of the MOF/COF scaffolds.
Confirm enzyme activity.
Mix lysozyme loaded MOFs/COFs with 4 mL of chitosan solution (0.6 mg/mL in 0.1 M acetate solution).
Add 1 mL of buffer (0.1 M acetate solution) to the mixture.
Seal the container and heat it in a preheated water bath at 50°C under constant magnetic stirring for 2 hours.
Remove pellets via filtration through a 0.45-μm membrane filter.
Add 1.5 mL of flow-through to 2.0 mL of coloring reagent (0.05% potassium ferricyanide solution).
Heat the mixture at 100°C for 15 minutes.
Determine optical intensity at 420 nm using a UV spectrometer upon cooling to room temperature.
Measure the decrease in OD420, which is proportional to the amount of reducing groups generated during chitosan hydrolysis by lysozyme.
Load samples to EPR capillaries.
Use minimal water volume for room temperature CW EPR measurement to avoid microwave power absorption by water molecular dipoles.
For most enzyme@MOF/COF materials, use a relatively larger total volume of ca. 20–40 μL for sufficient pellet effective volume in EPR measurement.
Use a pipette to load the large volume sample into EPR capillaries.
Turn on the CW EPR spectrometer.
Give sufficient time (5-10 min) for the electronics and cooling water to settle down/equilibrate.
Switch the bridge from the “STBY” mode to the “TUNE” mode.
Insert the sample tube into the cavity under low power (ca. 30 dB).
Observe a shift in the tuning dip when the sample is at the effective magnetic field region of the cavity.
Switch Reference Arm from “OFF” to “ABS”.
The phase of the tuning dip should be asymmetric under ABS Reference Arm.
Adjust PHASE to make the tuning dip symmetric.
Optimize the sample height and capillary position if the tuning dip position does not change.
Use a thinner capillary or increase the porous materials content if high water volume causes an issue.
Switch the Reference Arm to ABS.
The tuning dip should be asymmetric after switching to ABS.
Adjust the Iris to make the tuning dip symmetric.
Turn off the Reference Arm.
Switch to “Operate” mode.
Adjust the main frequency to center AFC OUT.
Tune the Reference Arm to ABS.
Adjust the Iris to center DET CUR.
Apply microwave power to the sample/cavity.
Slowly increase the power to 12 dB while adjusting the frequency to maintain the AFC OUT centered and the Iris to maintain the DET CUR centered.
Set up the EPR parameters.
Set up the initial center magnetic field for 9.6 GHz at approximately 3390 G.
Set the scan range to 100 G, which is often sufficient for HO-225 spin label and protein dynamics measurement at room temperature.
Set the modulation frequency to 100 KHz.
Start Video Gain at 160 and optimize based on signal strength.
Use a modulation depth of 1 G for nitroxide spin labels on protein studies at room temperature.
Run a test scan and optimize EPR parameters.
Adjust center field and Video Gain based on the test run.
Decrease modulation depth to 0.5 G to ensure linewidth is not narrowed.
Acquire a CW EPR spectrum via signal averaging until a satisfactory signal-to-noise ratio (usually >30) is reached.
Store all spectra electronically with documented parameters for further use.
Simulate EPR spectral data to extract dynamic information from acquired CW EPR spectra.
Consider the motion of the R1 spin label attached to an α helix as "anisotropic".
Document ranges of rate (τ) and order (S) parameters and their changes due to protein rotational tumbling.
Perform baseline correction on the EPR spectra using a 2nd–3rd order polynomial method.
Normalize the double-integration of the baseline-corrected spectra to 1 (or 100%).
Set up the initial fitting parameters.
Activate two components by switching the “Component” under A and B to “Enabled” while keeping components C and D “Disabled”.
Define component A as the spectrum contributed by enzyme in contact with (or immobilized on) the MOF/COF, while component B as the non-contact (or mobile) one.
Switch to the “Tensors” tab.
Input gxx=2.0078 for both “im” and “m” components in the “Tensors” Tab.
Input gyy=2.0058 for both “im” and “m” components in the “Tensors” Tab.
Input gzz=2.0023 for both “im” and “m” components in the “Tensors” Tab.
Input Axx= 5.7 G for both “im” and “m” components in the “Tensors” Tab.
Input Ayy=6.0 G for both “im” and “m” components in the “Tensors” Tab.
Activate green light after Azz input of 34.5 G for “im” component to allow variation during simulation.
Activate green light after Azz input of 37.5 G for “m” component to allow variation during simulation.
Set up parameters for spatial ordering and key Euler angles.
Specify the tilt of the diffusion tensor with respect to the molecular axis using Euler angles (αD, βD, γD).
For axially symmetric motion, specify only βD and γD.
For z-axis anisotropic motion, set the diffusion tilt at βD = 36° and γD = 0°.
Alter βD during simulation if a reasonable fit is not obtained with βD = 36°.
Switch βD to 90° and initiate fitting again if necessary.
Weight the low-field region of the spectrum by 50% for better fitting emphasis.
Carry out Levenberg-Marquardt fit to quickly determine parameters that best fit the spectrum.
Select Monte-Carlo fitting option to avoid local minima during fitting.
Determine enzyme dynamics to extract additional dynamic information.
Calculate ordering parameters C20 and C22 for the immobile component.
Interpret smaller ordering parameters as less spatial restriction at contact sites.
Relate ordering parameters to relative packing density of MOFs.
Analyze rate parameter to reflect dynamics of label at contact site.
Identify spin exchange interactions due to conjugated structure of building blocks.
Observe line broadening and spectral intensity changes for spin exchange indication.
Use specific spectral features to quantify exchange interaction in presence of spin exchange.
